Emergency care

Emergency care, S-CABCDE and look-alike conditions

Build a priority order for scene safety, life threats and a clear medical handover.

Official sources checked: 2026-09-19

Make the scene safe

Check traffic, violence, fire, weapons and environmental hazards before providing aid. A harmed responder cannot continue helping.

Use a structured sequence

S-CABCDE prioritises catastrophic bleeding, airway, breathing, circulation, disability and exposure. Follow the version taught in current official training.

01ASSIGNMENT02AUTHORITY03PROPORTION04REPORT

Conditions may be misread

Diabetes, epilepsy, stroke, mental distress, intoxication and head injury can affect behaviour. Observe, ask and prioritise medical help when indicated.

Call and hand over clearly

Give location, hazards, symptoms, times, actions and changes. Continue observation until ambulance staff or another responsible resource takes over.

Use this material for structure and review. Current Swedish Police law, training and operational instruction always control.
